authority.legal_name: Transport Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
authority.geography_type: dense harbour city across a deep natural harbour with a large archipelago of outlying islands
authority.home_waters_label: Victoria Harbour and Hong Kong's outlying islands

mandate.summary: The Transport Department plans, licenses and regulates all public transport in Hong Kong, including the franchised and licensed ferry network — Star Ferry across Victoria Harbour, the six major outlying-island routes, and dozens of in-harbour and kaito services. Ferry service licensing, fares and sustainability sit squarely in its remit.
current_priorities: Sustain viable ferry services to the outlying islands (licence renewals, fare arrangements)
Decarbonize ferries under the Hong Kong Climate Action Plan 2050 (electric ferry pilot scheme)
Integrate ferries with the MTR/bus network as part of public transport
Improve reliability, comfort and frequency on island and in-harbour routes

policy_targets.interim_target: Halve carbon emissions from the 2005 level before 2035
policy_targets.vision: Hong Kong Climate Action Plan 2050 — carbon neutrality before 2050

ferry_decarbonization.pilot_scheme: EPD/TD Pilot Scheme for electric ferries (electric for in-harbour routes; hybrid-electric for outlying-island routes)
ferry_decarbonization.green_ferry_study: Government Green Ferry study identifies electric in-harbour and hybrid outlying-island ferries as the path to notable air-quality and emissions gains
ferry_decarbonization.network_scale: ~95 licensed ferry routes (11 within Victoria Harbour, 84 serving other areas), incl. the six major outlying-island routes

policy_targets.relevance: Hong Kong has already chosen electric/hybrid ferries as the decarbonization path for an ageing diesel fleet, and is grappling with the cost of keeping island services viable. Zero-emission foiling vessels are faster, far more efficient per passenger-mile, and quieter — directly serving the Climate Action Plan 2050 target while improving island-service economics.

precedent.headline: Hong Kong runs one of the world's great public ferry networks — and has already committed to electrifying it.

existing_marine_network.operator: Licensed ferry operators (Star Ferry, Sun Ferry, HKKF and others) regulated by the Transport Department
existing_marine_network.modes: Cross-harbour Star Ferry, six major outlying-island routes, in-harbour routes, inter-island and kaito services
existing_marine_network.scale: ~95 licensed ferry routes; the outlying-island routes are a lifeline for island communities
existing_marine_network.decarbonization: Government electric-ferry pilot scheme underway; first electric vessels entering Victoria Harbour service
existing_marine_network.note: Ferries are a mainstream, beloved public mode here. The proposal upgrades and decarbonizes them — it does not introduce water transport.

viability_pressure.issue: Outlying-island ferry routes face fare pressure and licence-renewal uncertainty; operators struggle to fund fleet renewal
viability_pressure.relevance: A far more efficient zero-emission vessel improves the unit economics that keep island services running — a public-good argument the Department already makes.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the zero-emission foiling upgrade to a ferry network Hong Kong already runs at scale and is committed to electrifying. Foiling hulls are faster, near-silent, low-wake and roughly an order of magnitude more efficient per passenger-mile than the diesel fleet — improving both island-service economics and Climate Action Plan 2050 outcomes, while sitting alongside the heritage Star Ferry.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real ferry piers during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Network mirrors the licensed in-harbour and outlying-island piers.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The iconic cross-harbour Star Ferry run; foiling adds a quiet, zero-emission express tier alongside the heritage service.
Major outlying-island lifeline route; foiling cuts a ~35-60 min crossing materially.
Central to Mui Wo (Lantau) lifeline route.
Central to Lamma (Yung Shue Wan); dense commuter island route.

Aberdeen to Lamma (Sok Kwu Wan); southern-district island route.

regional_links.note: Hong Kong's network is overwhelmingly domestic (in-harbour + outlying islands). Cross-boundary Greater Bay Area ferry links (e.g. to Shenzhen/Zhuhai/Macau) exist but are out of the core proposal — domestic island and harbour service leads entirely.

links.note: Northern Lantau/Ma Wan residential route; domestic, optional extension of the home network.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every leg must be routed through navigable water with NO land crossings, threading one of the world's busiest harbours. Hand-curated waypoints required to respect the shipping fairways, traffic separation schemes, marine parks and typhoon shelters.

hazards.detail: The harbour is extremely busy with cross-harbour ferries, tugs, barges and ocean traffic. Route through marked fairways with strict no-foil/low-speed geofences across the cross-harbour ferry lanes; never cut across the main fairway at foiling speed.

hazards.hazard: East Lamma Channel & West Lamma Channel TSS
hazards.detail: Major container-ship traffic separation schemes south and west of the islands. Island legs to Lamma, Cheung Chau and Mui Wo must cross these channels at marked crossing points, perpendicular and clear of large-vessel lanes.

hazards.hazard: Kap Shui Mun / Ma Wan channel & bridges
hazards.detail: Routes toward Ma Wan/north Lantau pass under the Tsing Ma and Kap Shui Mun bridges through a regulated channel; follow the marked channel, displacement/no-foil where required.
Eastern-harbour and Lei Yue Mun legs must respect the Tathong Channel ocean-traffic lane.

hazards.hazard: Sha Chau & Lung Kwu Chau Marine Park / dolphins
hazards.detail: Western waters near north Lantau are a Chinese white dolphin marine park with speed/route restrictions; keep clear or transit slowly per marine-park rules.

hazards.hazard: Typhoon shelters (Causeway Bay, Aberdeen, Yau Ma Tei)
hazards.detail: Typhoon shelters are congested, slow-speed anchorages; any pier inside a shelter requires displacement/no-foil, low-wake approach.
Keep all geometry clear of the Kwai Tsing container-terminal approaches and turning basins.
